facts.fact: Article 153 provides a Governor for each state; the 7th Amendment (1956) lets one person be Governor of two or more states.
Article 154 vests the executive power of the state in the Governor.
The Governor is appointed by the President by warrant (Art 155), on the Canadian model.
The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Art 156) for five years and resigns to the President.
The Constitution lays down no procedure for removing a Governor.
A Governor must be a citizen and 35 years old (Art 157).
Under Art 158 a Governor holds no office of profit and the emoluments of a shared Governor are split among the states.
The Governor takes oath before the Chief Justice of the High Court (Art 159).
keys: Chief Justice of the High Court

facts.fact: Under Art 161 the Governor pardons offences against state law but cannot pardon a death sentence or a court-martial sentence.
The Governor appoints the Advocate General (Art 165).
All executive action of a state is taken in the Governor's name (Art 166).
The State Election Commissioner is removed only like a High Court judge; SPSC members are removed only by the President.
The Governor makes a special address at the first session of each year (Art 176).
The Governor nominates one-sixth of the Council from literature, science, art, co-operative movement and social service.
The Governor decides an MLA's disqualification under Art 192 on the Election Commission's opinion.
The Governor constitutes the State Finance Commission every five years.
A tribal welfare minister is required in Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; the 94th Amendment (2006) freed Bihar.
The Governor is Chancellor of state universities; Tamil Nadu and Kerala passed bills to change this.
Constitutional discretion: reserving a bill for the President and recommending President's Rule (UPSC 2014).
Governors have special responsibilities under Art 371 in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland (371A), Manipur, Sikkim and Karnataka (371J).
Situational discretion: choosing a CM in a hung Assembly and dismissing a ministry that has lost confidence.
Under Art 163(2) the Governor's decision on whether a matter is in his discretion is final.
Under Art 200 the Governor may assent, withhold, return (not a Money Bill) or reserve a bill.
Reservation is compulsory for a bill that would endanger the position of the High Court.
Under Art 201 the President may assent to or withhold a reserved bill, or ask for reconsideration (not a Money Bill); the House reconsiders within six months.
Article 213 ordinances need the President's instructions in certain cases, unlike Art 123.
Under Art 361 no criminal proceedings lie against a Governor during the term, and emoluments are not reduced (UPSC 2018).
Shamsher Singh (1974) held that the Governor acts on ministerial advice except in express discretion.
Rameshwar Prasad (2006) held the 2005 dissolution of the Bihar Assembly unconstitutional.
Nabam Rebia (2016): the Governor cannot summon or advance an Assembly session on his own (Arunachal Pradesh).
B.P. Singhal (2010) held that a Governor cannot be removed arbitrarily or for ideological disagreement.
State of Punjab (November 2023): a Governor who withholds assent must return the bill to the legislature.
State of Tamil Nadu v. Governor (8 April 2025) fixed one-month and three-month limits and deemed ten bills assented under Art 142.
The Presidential Reference opinion of 20 November 2025 (CJI B.R. Gavai) held courts cannot fix timelines or declare deemed assent.
Sarkaria Commission (1983-88): the Governor should be an eminent outsider, a detached figure, chosen after consulting the CM (UPSC 2019).
Punchhi Commission (2007-10): a fixed five-year term for Governors and removal by the state legislature.
S. Abdul Nazeer, a retired Supreme Court judge, has been Governor of Andhra Pradesh since 24 February 2023.
C.M. Trivedi was the first Governor of Andhra Pradesh (1956).
E.S.L. Narasimhan was the common Governor of AP and Telangana in 2014-19.
Biswabhusan Harichandan was the first Governor of residuary AP alone (July 2019).
The AP Raj Bhavan is at Vijayawada.
The CM is appointed by the Governor under Art 164; the Constitution lays down no procedure.
Under Art 163(1) the Council headed by the CM aids and advises the Governor except in discretion.
Under Art 163(3) advice given to the Governor cannot be inquired into in any court.
State ministers may not exceed 15% of the Assembly nor be fewer than 12 (Art 164(1A), 91st Amendment 2003).
Andhra Pradesh, with 175 MLAs, can have at most 26 ministers including the CM.
A member disqualified for defection cannot be a state minister (Art 164(1B)).
The state Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly (Art 164(2)).
A non-member may be a state minister for six months only (Art 164(4); UPSC 2020).
S.R. Chaudhuri (2001) bars re-appointing a non-member minister without election.
Article 167 makes it the CM's duty to communicate Cabinet decisions to the Governor.
Under Art 177 ministers and the Advocate General may speak in either House but vote only where members.
A Chief Minister may be a member of the Legislative Council.
The Constitution does not require a CM to prove majority before appointment; a floor test follows.
The Deputy CM post is not in the Constitution; the Supreme Court upheld such appointments in February 2024.
The CM chairs the State Planning Board and sits on the NITI Aayog Governing Council, the Inter-State Council and the Zonal Council.
The CM's death or resignation dissolves the state Council of Ministers.
The state Council has Cabinet ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
The Chief Secretary is chosen by the CM, not the Governor, and has no fixed tenure (UPSC 2016).
G. Sai Prasad became Chief Secretary of Andhra Pradesh on 28 February 2026.
N. Chandrababu Naidu (TDP, Kuppam) became AP CM on 12 June 2024, his fourth term.
Konidela Pawan Kalyan (Jana Sena, Pithapuram) is Deputy CM of Andhra Pradesh.
In the 2024 AP Assembly election the NDA won 164 of 175 (TDP 135, JSP 21, BJP 8); YSRCP 11; Congress 0.
Tanguturi Prakasam was the first CM of Andhra State (1953).
Neelam Sanjiva Reddy was the first CM of Andhra Pradesh (1956).
N.T. Rama Rao (TDP, 1983) was the first non-Congress CM of AP.
P.V. Narasimha Rao is the AP CM who later became Prime Minister.
The state legislature is in Part VI, Articles 168-212.
Six states have Councils: UP (100), Maharashtra (78), Bihar (75), Karnataka (75), AP (58), Telangana (40).
Uttar Pradesh has the largest Council (100); Telangana's (40) is the minimum size.
Councils were abolished in West Bengal (1969), Punjab (1970), Tamil Nadu (1986) and Jammu & Kashmir (2019).
Resolutions of Rajasthan, Assam and Odisha for new Councils await Parliament; MP's Council was never constituted.
Under Art 169 the Assembly passes a special-majority resolution and Parliament creates or abolishes the Council by simple-majority law, not an Art 368 amendment.
An Assembly has 60 to 500 members (Art 170); Sikkim 32, Goa and Mizoram 40 by special provision.
The Assembly term is five years (Art 172), extendable a year at a time in a National Emergency.
A Council may not exceed one-third of the Assembly and must have at least 40 (Art 171; UPSC 2015).
Council: 1/3 by local bodies, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated.
Graduate and teacher voters must be of three years' standing; teachers must teach not below secondary school.
The Council is permanent; one-third retire every 2 years and members serve 6 years (it is not dissolved).
Minimum age is 25 for the Assembly and 30 for the Council (Art 173).
The Council Chairman is elected by its members, not nominated by the Governor (UPSC 2015).
State legislature quorum is 10 members or one-tenth, whichever is greater (Art 189).
The Assembly Speaker is removed by an effective majority after 14 days' notice (Art 179) and stays after dissolution until the new Assembly meets.
Article 194 gives privileges to state legislators.
Art 211 bars discussion of judges' conduct; Art 212 bars courts from questioning legislature proceedings.
The Council can hold an Assembly bill three months the first time and one month the second — four months at most.
A bill from the Council that the Assembly rejects simply ends.
There is no joint sitting in a state legislature; the Assembly prevails.
A state Money Bill starts only in the Assembly on the Governor's recommendation; the Council has 14 days.
The Council has no role in electing the President or Rajya Sabha members; no-confidence lies only in the Assembly.
Article 202 provides for the state budget (Annual Financial Statement).
Absent its own rule, a state legislature does not have to follow Lok Sabha rules (UPSC 2019).
The 104th Amendment (2019) ended nomination of an Anglo-Indian to state Assemblies (Art 333).
A Council candidate must be an elector for an Assembly constituency; a Governor's nominee must reside in the state.
Lily Thomas (July 2013) made disqualification start from the date of conviction.
Defection disqualification in a state is decided by the Speaker or Chairman, not the Governor.
AP has 175 Assembly seats (undivided AP 294; Telangana 119).
Chintakayala Ayyanna Patrudu (TDP, Narsipatnam) was elected AP Speaker on 22 June 2024.
K. Raghu Rama Krishna Raju is Deputy Speaker of the AP Assembly.
AP Council of 58 = 20 by MLAs, 20 by local bodies, 5 graduates, 5 teachers, 8 nominated.
Koyye Moshenu Raju is Chairman of the AP Legislative Council.
The AP legislature sits at Amaravati (Velagapudi).
President's Rule was imposed in Andhra State (1954) and AP (1973, Jai Andhra; 2014).
The AP Council existed 1958-1985, was abolished in 1985 (NTR) and revived in 2007 (YSR).
AP's 2020 resolution to abolish the Council was withdrawn in November 2021 without a Parliament Act.
President's Rule does not necessarily dissolve the Assembly or local bodies (UPSC 2017).
